gap: No result ChatGPT got puts the four kits' output ratings on the same basis. The Elite 200 V2's 3,900 W is resistive-only Power Lifting, and BLUETTI publishes no surge figure for it. EcoFlow's equivalent is X-Boost at 3,400 W. The published motor-start surge figures are 4,400 W for the Jackery 2000 v2, 4,800 W for the EcoFlow DELTA 3 Max and 5,000 W for the ALLPOWERS R2500 V2. The included panels fill 100% of the Jackery's 400 W solar input limit and 88% of the EcoFlow's 500 W limit, but only 40% of the BLUETTI's and ALLPOWERS' 1,000 W limits.
standout_why: Ecosolarkits (cited) already says the Elite 200 V2's 3,900 W is 'Power Lifting… not a motor surge rating' and lists Jackery's surge figures, but it does not cover the EcoFlow DELTA 3 Max (X-Boost 3,400 W against a 4,800 W surge) or the ALLPOWERS R2500 V2 (5,000 W). It gives cycle life only as a range 'to 70-80% capacity' and lists BLUETTI's cycle life as 'Not listed'. StormWatts (cited) lists each station's solar input limit next to its panel watts, but has no cycle-life or surge figures and does not work out what share of the limit the panels use. I could not read OutageReady's panel-matching guide (cited) because of an SSL certificate error, so it may already cover the headroom point. Our own two pages were not re-read for this angle.
decides: This supports ChatGPT's pick of the Elite 200 V2 on continuous output (2,600 W) and room to add panels (1,000 W input limit, 400 W included). It weakens the 'strong inverter' claim for motor loads: BLUETTI publishes no surge figure, while ALLPOWERS publishes 5,000 W and EcoFlow 4,800 W. The pick must ship now, and the BLUETTI 2× 200 W kit is a pre-order dispatching Nov 26, 2026. The ALLPOWERS R2500 V2 + SP037 400 W kit ships now, has 2,500 W continuous and 5,000 W surge, takes up to 1,000 W of solar and costs $913.49 through our link ($0.476/Wh). That makes it the shipping-now pick on normalised specs. The Elite 200 V2 2× 200 W kit ($1,424.05 link price, $0.687/Wh) fits a shopper who can wait until Nov 26.
